# fits-js

> A TypeScript FITS parser with lazy random-access reads. Runs in Node, browsers, Bun, and Deno from a single browser-safe core with zero runtime dependencies.

Application code installs `@fits-js/core`. Opening a file reads only header blocks, and a region cutout reads only the bytes that region covers, including over HTTP `Range`.

## Getting started

- [Quickstart](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/quickstart/): install, open a file from disk, over HTTP, or from a browser input, read a cutout
- [Overview](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/): install, the code behind the landing-page render

## Guides

- [Reading a FITS file](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/reading-a-file/): NodeFileReader, cutouts, choosing an extension
- [Reading over HTTP](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/reading-over-http/): HttpRangeReader, caching, range fallback, options
- [Working with HDUs](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/working-with-hdus/): enumeration, HDU types, lookup by EXTNAME
- [Working with image data](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/working-with-image-data/): readImage, BITPIX scaling, BLANK handling, raw mode
- [Working with headers](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/working-with-headers/): FitsHeader accessors, indexed keywords, CONTINUE, HIERARCH
- [Error handling](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/guides/error-handling/): FitsError hierarchy, warnings channel, aborting
- [API reference](https://prustic.github.io/fits-js/api/): auto-generated from TSDoc
